Present:- Mr. C.S. Rawat, Ms. Anjali Benjwal Bahuguna, and Mr. V.S. Rawat,
 Advocates for the petitioners.
 Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Advocate for respondent no. 1/Uttarakhand Open
 University.
 Mr. Vikas Pande, Advocate for respondent no. 2/University Grants
 Commission.

Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
 Miscellaneous application (IA No.10917/2019)
filed in WPMS No. 2393 of 2019 is allowed. Counter affidavit
filed on behalf of the respondent is taken on record.
2. Since the issue raised in all the aforesaid writ
petitions is common and identical, therefore, all these writ
petitions are heard together and decided by this common

4
judgment. However, for the sake of convenience, the facts of
Writ Petition (M/S) No.1542 of 2019 will be considered.
3. In this bunch of writ petitions, the petitioners
before this Court are running study centers of the
Uttarakhand Open University. All of them have now been
closed down by the order of the Uttarakhand Open University,
which has been passed in view of the Regulations made by the
University Grants Commission (from hereinafter referred to as
the "UGC") in the year 2017.
4. Distance education and the Open University
movement came in India with the purpose to provide formal
education for those who were deprived of obtaining the same
due to poverty or other challenges which they were facing in
their life. It is also a boon for those who could not afford to
enroll as regular students. This opportunity was given to them
to avail education through distance learning. It has benefited a
large section of the population.
5. In Uttarakhand, the Open University Act came in
the year 2005. Under Section 4 of the Uttaranchal Open
University Act, 2005, the objects of the University are given,
which reads as under:-
 "Section 4. The University shall
promote dissemination of learning and
knowledge through distance education
systems including the use of any
communication technology to provide
opportunities for higher education to a large
segment of the population and shall, in
organizing it's activities, have due regard to the
objects specified in the first schedule."
6. In order to be effective mode of learning and not
just a formality, studies centers were encouraged by the

5
Uttarakhand Open University, which are opened at various
distant places.
7. The UGC in its Regulations of the year 2003 has
defined the "study center" in clause 2.4, which is as follows:-
 "2.4. "study centre" means a centre
established and maintained or recognized by
the university for the purpose of advising,
counseling or for rendering any other
assistance required by the students used in
the context of distance education."
8. These study centers are being run by private
bodies. The purpose is to help students who were taking the
education through distance mode, in preparation of their
courses and tutorials.
9. The UGC now in the year 2017 has come out
with new Regulations, which is known as University Grants
Commission (Open and Distance Learning) Regulations, 2017.
Clause 14 of the said Regulations reads as under:-
 "14. Learner Support Centre
 (1)A Higher Educational Institution
offering programme in Open and Distance mode
shall, within one year from the date of
commencement of these regulations, ensure that
a Learned Support Centre is established only in a
college or institution affiliated to a University or
in a government recognized Higher Educational
Institution offering programmed in the same
broad areas having the necessary infrastructure
and human resources for offering the
programme.
 Provided that a Higher Education
Institution may establish a special Learner
Support Centre for imparting instruction to
persons referred to in the Persons with
Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of
Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995, the
National Trust for Welfare of Persons with
Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation and

6
Multiple Disability Act, 1999 and other persons
in difficult circumstances, including jail inmates:
 Provided further that a Learner
Support Centre shall not be set up under a
franchisee agreement in any case.
 (2) A Learner Support Centre shall be
the contact point or centre managed by the
Higher Educational Institution for providing
academic as well as administrative support to its
learners, and shall perform such other functions
as specified in Annexure X.
 (3) The Learner Support Centre shall
be headed by a Coordinator who shall be a
regular teacher not below the rank of a qualified
Assistant Professor of the concerned College or
Higher Educational Institution and assisted by
the counselors as decided by the Higher
Educational Institution.
 (4) The Higher Educational
Institution shall have a Standard Operating
Procedure for the smooth functioning of the
Learner Support Centre which shall include
functions of the Learner Support Centres and its
different functionaries, monitoring mechanism of
different services provided by the Centre, and it
shall be mandatory for the Learner Support
Centre to maintain the learner data related to
conduct of counseling sessions, evaluation of
assignments and grievance redressal."
10. Clause 15 of the Regulations of 2017 reads as
under:-
 "15. Learner Support Services-
 (1) A Higher Educational Institution
offering programmed in Open and Distance
Learning mode shall have guidelines for learner
support services which is made available to all
Learner Support Centres and accessible to the
learners.
 (2) The learner support services to be
provided by the Higher Educational Institution
shall include the following namely:-
 (i) pre-admission counselling for
prospective learners to provide information to

7
facilitate them in taking an informed decision
on joining a specific programme;
 (ii) support for admission related matters;
 (iii) details of study material and
information shall also be available on the
website of the Higher Educational Institution;
 (iv) arrangement to ensure the delivery of
study material to learners within a fortnight
from the date of admission.
 (v) A full time dedicated help desk well
versed with the learner information data base
providing single window services for all
learner related queries.
 (3) The University Grants Commission
(Grievance Redressal) Regulations, 2012 shall be
adopted and operationalised by the Higher
Educational Institution, and the Higher
Educational Institution shall institute a system of
Grievance Redressal, in accordance with the
guidelines specified in Annexure XI.
 (4) The Higher Educational Institution
shall provide facilities for on-line guidance and
counselling facilities to the learners.
 (5) The Higher Educational Institution
shall create 'on-line' discussion forum for
learners.
 (6) The 'Self Learning Material' in printed
form shall be provided compulsorily to the
learners and in addition, the Higher Educational
Institution may provide additional learning
resources through on-line mode, Compact Disks,
etc."
11. A bare perusal of the aforesaid Regulations
shows that any higher education institution which would
include an Open University such as Uttarakhand Open
University, and which is offering programme in open and
distance mode, shall within one year from the date of
commencement of these Regulations, ensure that a Learner
Support Centre, which means a study center, is henceforth

8
established only in a college or Institution, affiliated to a
University, or in a government recognized Higher Educational
Institution offering programmes in the same broad areas,
which have the necessary infrastructure and human resources
for offering the programme.
12. The aforesaid provision was included in order to
make the study centers more effective tools of learning by
means of distance education. In view of the aforesaid
provision, the petitioner started getting instructions from the
Uttarakhand Open University to make the necessary changes.
The first letter which the petitioner had received was on
04.12.2017 asking the petitioner to get itself affiliated to a
University or a recognized higher educational institution in
order to fulfill the requirements as contained in Regulations of
2017 and update its study center as per the Regulations.
13. Learned counsel for the Uttarakhand Open
University as well as the learned counsel for the UGC have
informed this Court that although the orders were received by
the petitioner but he did not even bother to file his reply to the
same. Thereafter another notice was given to the petitioner on
14.08.2018 reminding him that it should complete the
formalities and get itself affiliated to a University. This too
went in vain. Again on 21.08.2018 and 17.10.2018 notices
were given to the petitioner and finally an order was passed on
24.01.2019, wherein it was found that the study center of the
petitioner is not affiliated to a University and therefore after
31.12.2018, the Open University has stopped the recognition
of the study center of the petitioner as a recognized body.
Aggrieved, the petitioners have filed the present writ petitions
before this Court.

9
14. Learned counsel for the petitioners would argue
that Regulations of 2017 which have been framed by the UGC
are in violation of Section 26 (2) of the University Grants
Commission Act, 1956. Section 26 of the University Grants
Commission Act, 1956 reads as under:-
 "Section 26. (1) The Commission may, by
notification in the Official Gazette, make
regulations consistent with this Act and the
rules made thereunder-
(a) regulating the meetings of the Commission
and the procedure for conducting business
thereat;
(b) regulating the manner in which and the
purposes for which persons may be
associated with the Commission under
section 9;
(c) specifying the terms and conditions of
service of the employees appointed by the
Commission;
(d) specifying the institutions or class of
institutions which may be recognised by the
Commission under clause (f) of sub-section
2;
(e) defining the qualifications that should
ordinarily be required of any person to be
appointed to the teaching staff of the
University, having regard to the branch of
education in which he is expected to give
instruction;
(f) defining the minimum standards of
instruction for the grant of any degree by
any University;
(g) regulating the maintenance of standards
and the co-ordination of work or facilities in
Universities.
(h) regulating the establishment of institutions
referred to in clause (ccc) of section 12 and
other matters relating to such institutions;
(i) specifying the matters in respect of which
fees may be charged, and scales of fees in
accordance with which fees may be charged,
by a college under sub-section (2) of section
12A;
(j) specifying the manner in which an inquiry
may be conducted under sub-section (4) of
section 12A;

10
 (2) No regulation shall be made under
clause (a) or clause (b) or clause (c) or clause (d)
or clause (h) or clause (j) or clause (j) of sub-section (1) except with the previous approval of
the Central Government.
 (3) The power to make regulations
conferred by this section except clause (i) and
clause (j) of sub-section (1) shall include the
power to give retrospective effect from a date not
earlier than the date of commencement of this
Act, to the regulations or any of them but no
retrospective effect shall be given to any
regulation so as to prejudicially affect the
interests of any person to whom such regulation
may be applicable."
 (Emphasis provided)
15. Learned counsel for the petitioners would rely
upon sub-section (2) of Section 26 of the University Grants
Commission Act, 1956 and would argue that the Regulations
i.e. (Regulations of the year 2017) have been made without
previous approval of the Central Government. Although there
is no specific pleading taken by the petitioner in the writ
petition in this regard and therefore there is no formal reply on
this either by the UGC or by the Uttarakhand Open University,
but the fact remains that in any case there was no
requirement for taking any previous approval of the Central
Government under Section 26 of the University Grants
Commission Act, 1956 as Regulations apparently have been
passed under sub-section (1)(g) of Section 26 of the University
Grants Commission Act, 1956. For regulating the minimum
standard and the coordination of work or facilities in the
University, it does not have to take the prior sanction of the
University. Sanction of the University is to be taken for other
provisions which is given in clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (h), (i) or (j)
of sub-section (1) of Section 26 of the University Grants
Commission Act, 1956, which is not the case here.

11
16. Moreover, the Regulations of 2017 and the
subsequent orders which have been passed by the
Uttarakhand Open University are in pith and substance for
better education and learning. The purpose is to raise the
standard for learning.
17. The grievance of the petitioners is that they have
spent more than one lakh rupees in building these study
centers. The other argument of the petitioners would be that
before setting up the study centers, they have fulfilled all the
norms and now effectively these study centers have been made
non-functional.
18. There is nothing static in law or life. The study
centers which were opened by the petitioners at the relevant
time were in accordance with law, but now they have simply
been asked to improve their standards, which is the mandate
of the Regulations of 2017 and there is nothing wrong in it.
Rather it has a good purpose which is to improve the standard
of education. The Regulations are to be followed by the
Uttarakhand Open University. It is the petitioners which have
not followed the instructions inasmuch as they have not got
themselves affiliated to a University as it was required under
the Regulations of 2017. Therefore, if the recognition has been
taken away from the petitioners by the Uttarakhand Open
University, no fault can be found in it.
19. These writ petitions therefore have no merit and
are hereby dismissed. Interim order, if any, stands vacated.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 21.08.2019
Ankit/
